_comment: The changelog. tools/changelog.py renders CHANGELOG.md from this file, and release notes and the installer's changelog are written from it. Every user-visible change edits this file in the same commit. Statuses: new/fix (in a release, seen working in game), beta (merged, not yet verified in game), next (still being built, not merged).
intro:
Every change to XivDesktop a player can see, newest first.

XivDesktop has not yet been observed running in the game: host tests cover the catalog, search, the calculator, key chords, workspaces and the IPC payloads, and nothing below about in-game behaviour has been seen working. Treat it as the design, not as a result — the README says the same thing.

releases.title: In the workshop
releases.blurb: Everything here is merged into master. BETA means exactly that and no more: merged, and not yet seen working in the game.

items.text: `/arcade`: a library of your own classic games, Final Fantasy first, that start in RetroArch on the Linux host and show up as a game panel. `/arcade ff7` plays the closest match, `/arcade last` resumes, and the palette finds games by name. The first run is three steps that tick themselves off, above a text-only Final Fantasy shelf that lights up as your files appear; a LaunchBox folder can be copied in as it is. Every save and save state lives in one folder that Syncthing copies between your machines: a game never starts while saves are still arriving, a conflict keeps both saves with the newer one live, and `/arcade import-saves` never overwrites a newer save. XivDesktop downloads no games, BIOS files or artwork, installs nothing and pairs no device; it shows the command for each step. Not yet seen in game, with a real emulator, or syncing between two machines; FFXIV also reacts to the controller while you play. See docs/ARCADE.md.

releases.blurb: BETA entries are in this release but have not been verified in game yet; they become NEW or FIX once they have been seen working.

items.text: In progress: the `/npc` speaker's body. The dialogue works, but the character never appears in the world yet. The speaker is now built with the game's own creature setup (nothing is copied from your character: no gear, no name, no company tag), and every step reports to the Dalamud log, which is how the cause was narrowed down. What was tried and what to try next is in docs/NPC-SPAWN.md.

releases.title: Released 2026-09-20
releases.blurb: BETA entries are in this release but have not been verified in game yet; they become NEW or FIX once they have been seen working.

items.text: XivDesktop itself: a launcher for your Linux desktop's apps inside the game. `/desktop` opens an app grid with icons, favourites and recent apps; the apps run on the Linux host, not inside Wine, and appear as game panels through a compatible Ghostty for Dalamud build and its host agent. XivDesktop does not render or stream windows itself.
A keyboard-first launcher palette (Super+D by default, configurable): search apps and open panels, run actions, or type a sum into a bounded calculator.
Key chords, nine workspaces, and focus, close and placement controls for panels, through Ghostty's IPC. Advanced operations need the matching methods in the installed Ghostty build.
Optional Umbra toolbar widgets: Apps (a launcher) and Windows (a taskbar). Both are clients of XivDesktop's IPC and neither replaces the Ghostty backend.
Experimental: `/npc <question>` summons a local speaker with a Talk-style dialogue, answered by Almanac's local gateway; `/npc bye` dismisses it and `/npc who` opens the picker.

Experimental: `/claude` opens a Claude Code session as an in-game panel, with streaming text, tool cards and permission dialogs, run as Ghostty agent jobs. It has its own backend, sign-in and data handling, separate from Almanac's local models.
The game's cursor stays visible over XivDesktop's windows and popups.
